requirements.text: Start from https://books.toscrape.com/ and crawl only the first three categories of the side list.
Visit every book each category lists, following the category's "next" pages.
Extract each book's title, price, number in stock and star rating with a language model (no hand-written field selectors), and keep each extracted book (dataset or output).
Ask the model once per page type: later books of the same layout are extracted from what was learned with no model call, and a page that no longer matches what was learned goes back to the model.
Stop all model use once a set spend (e.g. 0.50 USD) is reached, and let the crawl finish without the model (learned extraction still working).
Report which books were left unextracted and why (budget reached, extraction or request failure).
Report the tokens and the cost spent on the model.

site_errors: side list selector uses div.side-categories; the class is side_categories
programs.notes: page.extract (compiled, Run's Plan) learns once and repairs on Drift, ai.allowance.price caps spend with skipped/model_allowance outcomes; unextracted books come from run.outcomes keyed by request ID and tokens/price from report.usage.model. The Run is not disposed itself but the connection's disposal closes it.

Same engine-backed design as the golden: compiled extract, price allowance, unextracted books from outcomes (skipped/failed/blocked) read after finish, usage and price from the report; the extra lock is harmless.

Extraction, allowance and usage reporting are right, but unextracted books are tallied only from errors returned inside the book handler, so book requests that fail or are blocked before the handler are only counted, never listed with a reason. The fixed Run id makes a second invocation resume the ended Run and do nothing.

PydanticAiSelectorExtractor learns selectors per label and relearns on mismatch, a WrapperModel refuses requests past the budget (check-then-charge, like the reference leader), unextracted books come from the handler and failed_request_handler, tokens from crawler.ai_usage and cost from genai-prices with a flat fallback rate.

One observe learns XPaths for all four fields, later books are read with Playwright and relearned on a failed read, model calls are serialized and metered from stagehand.metrics against a hand price table, and unextracted books come with reasons from the handler and failedRequestHandler.

Compiled extract with the Run's Plan and a price allowance; the module-level first-compile gate is redundant with the engine's own but harmless. Unextracted books come from outcomes of the book Label, and usage and price from the report.

Sync API: compiled extract with handler concurrency 1, a price allowance, unextracted books from outcomes of the book Label after finish, tokens and cost from report.usage.model; the connection's with-block closes the Run.
Compiled extract, allowance and handler concurrency 1, served to the end; unextracted books come from run.outcomes filtered to the book Label, and tokens/cost from the Run's usage after serving.

Selector extractor and budgeted WrapperModel are used correctly, but there is no failed_request_handler: book requests that fail to fetch are only counted (stats.requests_failed), never listed with a reason. It also catches every extraction error, so a provider outage is reported rather than retried, and an unpriced response stops all model use.

The first book of a layout goes to page.extract, then CSS paths are found by matching the model's values, later books are read from them, and the model is called again under a serialized budget check when no recipe matches. But the extracted books are kept only in an in-memory map and never pushed to a Dataset or printed, so the extracted data is lost; only counts are reported.
